summary: Accepted distribution design decision. The intended v0.1 primary path is single-file executables per OS built by bun build --compile and attached to GitHub Releases; the ADR describes plans, not proof that release artifacts, signing, checksums, or updates have shipped. It also plans a self-updater with SHA-256 verification against a minisign-signed checksum file, atomic replacement, and passive notices only; later Tauri installers and package-manager options; and secondary npm packages and npx. Why: one executable simplifies setup without requiring separate Node or Git installs; GitHub Releases offers bandwidth and reaches the audience. Consequences describe a planned release matrix, checksum/signature publication, unsigned Windows SmartScreen warnings, provenance and integrity guidance, and accepted binary size.

sections.title: Decision
sections.summary: The intended v0.1 primary distribution is a single-file executable for each listed OS and architecture, built with bun build --compile and attached to GitHub Releases. Planned vaud upgrade behavior checks a downloaded binary against SHA-256 values in a minisign-signed checksum file before atomic replacement; notices stay passive and installs require consent. Tauri installers and package managers are later options; npm packages and npx remain secondary. This is an accepted design, not evidence those artifacts or mechanisms have shipped.

sections.title: Why
sections.summary: A single executable simplifies setup by avoiding separate Node and Git installation. The accepted plan uses bun build --compile to make that path practical across the named operating systems. GitHub Releases offers a distribution channel with bandwidth and reaches the intended audience; this decision does not claim that binaries have already shipped.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.summary: The ADR plans a per-tag binary matrix with checksums and signatures; these are planned release requirements, not confirmation of published artifacts. Unsigned Windows executables may trigger SmartScreen. Distribution guidance should disclose signing status and show users how to check provenance and integrity, without presenting a blanket bypass as safe. The expected 50–90 MB size from the embedded Bun runtime is accepted and should be documented.
